prompt: School bus pre-trip inspection should include checking

options.text: Lights, mirrors, emergency exits, tires, brakes, and required safety equipment
Engine fluids and tires, with lights and mirrors checked on arrival at the school
Brakes and tires, leaving emergency exits for the monthly drill
Lights and mirrors, with brakes left to the mechanic's weekly test

explanation: A thorough pre-trip verifies systems that protect students and road users before departure.

distractorExplanations.b: Lights and mirrors are checked before leaving the lot; a bus cannot begin a route with misadjusted mirrors or dead warning lights.
distractorExplanations.c: Emergency exits are part of every pre-trip; evacuation drills are separate from confirming the exits open and their alarms work.
distractorExplanations.d: Brake checks are part of the driver's pre-trip every day; a weekly mechanic check does not replace them.

prompt: Convex (fisheye) mirrors on a school bus are used primarily to:

options.text: Show the area directly in front of the bumper, which crossover mirrors cannot
Show wide areas along the sides and front danger zones that flat mirrors may miss
Show the true distance and size of vehicles beside the bus for lane changes
Show the area behind the bus so backing is safe without a lookout

explanation: Convex mirrors expand field of view for loading-zone and side blind spots; drivers still must scan properly.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses convex with crossover mirrors; crossover mirrors cover the area in front of the bumper, while convex mirrors cover the sides.
distractorExplanations.c: Convex mirrors make objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are, so they do not show true distance.
distractorExplanations.d: Convex mirrors do not show directly behind the bus; backing still needs a responsible lookout and extreme caution.

prompt: The danger zone around a school bus is generally considered

The road ahead between where the amber lights start and where the red lights activate

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses the danger zone with traffic stopping distances; the danger zone is the area around the bus where students are struck.

prompt: If an emergency exit warning buzzer sounds because a door/window is open while driving, you should
